newsitem.title: USA: Taro gets glaucoma, epilepsy drug okay.
newsitem.headline: Taro gets glaucoma, epilepsy drug okay.

text.p: Taro Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd said on Monday that it has received notification from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approving its Abbreviated New Drug Application for acetazolamide Tablets, in strengths of 125 mg and 250 mg.
According to Taro, the drug has several therapeutic applications, including the treatment of glaucoma and certain types of epilepsy.
Taro's acetazolamide tablets are bioequivalent to Diamoxr Tablets, which are made by American Home Products Corp's Lederle Laboratories.
The company said it will manufacture acetazolamide tablets at its facilities in Haifa, Israel.
